# Overview

Runs the Mandarin extraction from CHILDES utterances through token-level negation coding to `mandarin_data/processed_data/mandarin_tokens_processed.feather`. Uses `mandarin` as the working directory with `childesr`, `tidyverse`, and `arrow`, and reuses corpus caches unless `mandarin_force_download` is `TRUE`.

# Setup

Loads `childesr`, `tidyverse`, and `arrow`, configures knitr, and creates `mandarin_raw_dir` and `mandarin_processed_dir`.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  error = FALSE,
  cache = FALSE
)
library(childesr)
library(tidyverse)
library(arrow)
```

```{r directories}
mandarin_db_version <- "2026.1"
mandarin_force_download <- FALSE

mandarin_data_root <- "mandarin_data"

mandarin_raw_dir <- file.path(mandarin_data_root, "raw_data")
mandarin_processed_dir <- file.path(mandarin_data_root, "processed_data")

dir.create(mandarin_raw_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(mandarin_processed_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

# Load Data

Selects CHILDES source corpora and imports utterances into `mandarin_all_utterances` for annotation.

## Select Corpora

Selects 20 Mandarin corpora in `mandarin_corpora_names` for CHILDES release `mandarin_db_version`.

```{r collections}
# This chunk specifies the 20 Mandarin corpora included in the data request.
mandarin_corpora_names <- c(
  "AcadLang",
  "BJCMC",
  "Chang1",
  "Chang2",
  "ChangPlay",
  "ChangPN",
  "Erbaugh",
  "LiReading",
  "LiZhou",
  "NSCtoys",
  "TCCM",
  "TCCM-reading",
  "Tong",
  "Xinjiang",
  "Zhou1",
  "Zhou2",
  "Zhou3",
  "ZhouAssessment",
  "ZhouDinner",
  "ZhouNarratives"
)
```

## Import Data

Downloads or reuses corpus-level Mandarin utterances in `mandarin_all_utterances` and checks the combined batch row count.

```{r import_utterances}
# Assumes mandarin_raw_dir, mandarin_db_version,
# mandarin_corpora_names, and mandarin_force_download are defined.

# One folder for this DB version, one Feather file per corpus.
mandarin_batch_dir <- file.path(
  mandarin_raw_dir,
  paste0("corpus_batches_", mandarin_db_version, "_all_speakers")
)

dir.create(mandarin_batch_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

mandarin_batch_files <- file.path(
  mandarin_batch_dir,
  paste0(mandarin_corpora_names, ".feather")
)

# Columns every corpus file must have.
mandarin_required_columns <- c(
  "id", "transcript_id", "target_child_id", "target_child_age",
  "gloss", "speaker_role", "speaker_code", "type", "utterance_order",
  "part_of_speech"
)

# A saved batch is usable if the file exists and has the required columns.
mandarin_batch_is_valid <- function(path) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(FALSE)
  saved_columns <- names(arrow::open_dataset(path, format = "ipc"))
  all(mandarin_required_columns %in% saved_columns)
}

# Write to a temporary file first, then rename it.
# If R stops mid-write, no half-written batch is left behind.
mandarin_save_batch <- function(data, path) {
  temp_path <- paste0(path, ".tmp")
  arrow::write_feather(data, temp_path)
  if (!file.rename(temp_path, path)) stop("Could not save: ", path)
}

mandarin_download_status <- tibble::tibble(
  corpus_name = mandarin_corpora_names,
  status = "pending",
  n_utterances = NA_real_,
  error = NA_character_
)

for (i in seq_along(mandarin_corpora_names)) {
  corpus_name <- mandarin_corpora_names[[i]]
  path <- mandarin_batch_files[[i]]
  message(sprintf("[%d/%d] %s", i, length(mandarin_corpora_names), corpus_name))

  if (!mandarin_force_download && mandarin_batch_is_valid(path)) {
    # Already saved: reuse it and just count its rows.
    mandarin_download_status$status[[i]] <- "cached"
    mandarin_download_status$n_utterances[[i]] <-
      nrow(arrow::read_feather(path, col_select = "id"))

  } else {
    # Not saved yet: download all speakers (no role argument).
    # tryCatch turns an error into a message so the loop moves on.
    utts <- tryCatch(
      childesr::get_utterances(
        corpus = corpus_name,
        db_version = mandarin_db_version
      ),
      error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
    )

    if (is.character(utts)) {
      # Download failed: utts holds the error message.
      mandarin_download_status$status[[i]] <- "failed"
      mandarin_download_status$error[[i]] <- utts
      message("  FAILED: ", utts)
    } else {
      mandarin_save_batch(utts, path)
      mandarin_download_status$status[[i]] <- "downloaded"
      mandarin_download_status$n_utterances[[i]] <- nrow(utts)
      message("  Saved ", nrow(utts), " utterances.")
    }
  }
}

if (any(mandarin_download_status$status == "failed")) {
  stop(
    "Some corpora failed. Completed batches remain saved. ",
    "Keep mandarin_force_download <- FALSE and rerun this chunk."
  )
}

mandarin_all_utterances <- mandarin_batch_files %>%
  purrr::map(arrow::read_feather) %>%
  purrr::keep(function(d) nrow(d) > 0) %>%
  dplyr::bind_rows()

# The combined data should have exactly as many rows as the batches.
stopifnot(
  nrow(mandarin_all_utterances) ==
    sum(mandarin_download_status$n_utterances)
)

mandarin_download_status %>%
  dplyr::select(corpus_name, status, n_utterances)
```

# Token Processing

Filters `mandarin_utterances` by `target_child_age` and assigns speaker, age, and utterance-type fields before negation coding.

## Filter Ages and Count Exclusions

Filters `mandarin_all_utterances` to finite `target_child_age` values from 0 to under 72 months and records row and child counts in `mandarin_exclusions`.

```{r exclusions}
mandarin_n_utterances_before_exclusions <- nrow(mandarin_all_utterances)
mandarin_n_chi_before_exclusions <- mandarin_all_utterances$target_child_id %>%
  unique() %>% length()

mandarin_utterances <- mandarin_all_utterances %>%
  filter(is.finite(target_child_age))

mandarin_n_utterances_after_finite_age <- nrow(mandarin_utterances)
mandarin_n_chi_after_finite_age <- mandarin_utterances$target_child_id %>%
  unique() %>% length()

mandarin_utterances <- mandarin_utterances %>%
  filter(target_child_age >= 0, target_child_age < 72)

mandarin_n_utterances_after_age_range <- nrow(mandarin_utterances)
mandarin_n_chi_after_age_range <- mandarin_utterances$target_child_id %>%
  unique() %>% length()

mandarin_exclusions <- tibble(
  n_utterances_before_exclusions = mandarin_n_utterances_before_exclusions,
  n_after_finite_age = mandarin_n_utterances_after_finite_age,
  n_after_age_range = mandarin_n_utterances_after_age_range,
  missing_or_nonfinite_age =
    mandarin_n_utterances_before_exclusions - mandarin_n_utterances_after_finite_age,
  outside_age_range =
    mandarin_n_utterances_after_finite_age - mandarin_n_utterances_after_age_range,
  n_chi_total = mandarin_n_chi_before_exclusions,
  n_chi_after_finite_age = mandarin_n_chi_after_finite_age,
  n_chi_after_age_range = mandarin_n_chi_after_age_range
)

mandarin_exclusions
```

## Save Exclusion Records

Saves `mandarin_exclusions` and the age-filtered `mandarin_utterances` as CSV files in `mandarin_raw_dir`.

```{r save_exclusions}
readr::write_csv(
  mandarin_exclusions,
  file.path(mandarin_raw_dir, "exclusions_mandarin_summary.csv")
)
readr::write_csv(
  mandarin_utterances,
  file.path(mandarin_raw_dir, "mandarin_utterances_excluded.csv")
)
```

## Assign Speaker Roles

Maps target-child roles to `child` and every other role, including missing values, to `parent` in `mandarin_utterances$speaker`.

```{r speaker_roles}
mandarin_utterances <- mandarin_utterances %>%
  mutate(
    speaker = case_when(
      str_to_lower(as.character(speaker_role), locale = "en") == "target_child" ~ "child",
      TRUE ~ "parent"
    )
  )
```

## Calculate Age in Months

Calculates `mandarin_utterances$age` as the floor of `target_child_age` in months.

```{r age}
mandarin_utterances$age <- mandarin_utterances$target_child_age %>% floor()
```

## Recode Utterance Types

Recodes question, imperative, and disrupted labels from `type` into `mandarin_utterances$utterance_type`, leaving unlisted values unchanged.

```{r utterance_types}
# Prepare the utterance_type categories for this study based on the utterance_types in childes-db
## Categories: declarative, imperative, interrogative, and other
mandarin_utterances$utterance_type <-
  dplyr::recode(
    as.character(mandarin_utterances$type),
    question = "interrogative",
    `broken for coding` = "other",
    imperative_emphatic = "imperative",
    interruption = "other",
    `interruption question` = "interrogative",
    `missing CA terminator` = "other",
    `no break TCU continuation` = "other",
    `question exclamation` = "interrogative",
    `quotation next line` = "other",
    `quotation precedes` = "other",
    `self interruption` = "other",
    `self interruption question` = "interrogative",
    `trail off` = "other",
    `trail off question` = "interrogative"
  )
```

# Define Target Words

Defines Mandarin candidate negators and non-negating expression lists, then flags negation in `mandarin_utterances`.

## List Candidate Negators

Lists `不` and `没` in `mandarin_function_words` as candidate negators.

```{r function_words}
mandarin_function_words <- c(
  # Negation (no/not)
  "不","没"
)
```


## Define Excluded Expressions

Defines `bu_exclusion` and `mei_exclusion` as expressions whose negator characters should be ignored.

```{r mandarin_exclusionword}
# Special combinations that are not considered negation
bu_exclusion <- c(
  # Connectives: exclude these connective readings.
  "不过",     # however / merely
  "不過",     # however / merely (traditional)
  "不然",     # otherwise
  "要不然",   # otherwise
  "要不",     # otherwise / how about

  # Approximation or possibility.
  "差不多",   # approximately / almost
  "说不定",   # perhaps
  "說不定",   # perhaps (traditional)
  "搞不好",   # perhaps

  # Conventional social formulas.
  "对不起",   # sorry
  "對不起",   # sorry (traditional)
  "不客气",   # you're welcome
  "不客氣",   # you're welcome
  "不好意思", # excuse me / sorry

  # Intensification or conventional affirmation.
  "不得了",   # extremely / extraordinary
  "不错",     # good / correct
  "不錯",     # good / correct
  "可不"      # exactly / indeed
)

mei_exclusion <- c(
  "没关系", # that's all right / no relationship
  "沒關係", # that's all right / no relationship (traditional)
  "没错", # that’s right
  "沒錯", # that’s right 
  "没事",   # no problem / nothing happening
  "沒事",   # no problem (traditional)
  "没了",   # all gone / used up
  "沒了",   # all gone / used up (traditional)
  "熊出没" # name of Chinese cartoon
)
```

## Detect Negation

Builds `mandarin_exclusion_pattern` and `mandarin_a_not_a_pattern` to remove excluded phrases while retaining A-not-A questions. Flags remaining negators in `mandarin_utterances$negation`.

```{r mandarin_exclusion_pipeline}
# Negator characters: 不, simplified 没, traditional 沒
mandarin_negators <- "[不没沒]"

# Turn a phrase into a pattern that allows spaces between its characters:
# "对不起" -> "对 ?不 ?起", which matches 对不起, 对 不 起, 对不 起
phrase_pattern <- function(phrase) {
  paste(str_split_1(phrase, ""), collapse = " ?")
}

# Put longer phrases first so 要不然 is tried before 要不.
mandarin_exclusion_phrases <- unique(c(bu_exclusion, mei_exclusion))
mandarin_exclusion_phrases <- mandarin_exclusion_phrases[
  order(nchar(mandarin_exclusion_phrases), decreasing = TRUE)
]

mandarin_exclusion_regex <- map_chr(mandarin_exclusion_phrases, phrase_pattern)

# Special case for 不过: only joined 不过 is the connective ("however").
# Split 不 过 is always verb + 不过 = "can't beat / can't get past" (打 不 过).
# because 不 过 来 / 不 过 去 means "not come/go over" (real negation).
mandarin_exclusion_regex[mandarin_exclusion_phrases == "不过"] <- "不过"
mandarin_exclusion_regex[mandarin_exclusion_phrases == "不過"] <- "不過"
mandarin_exclusion_regex[mandarin_exclusion_phrases == "要不"] <- "要 ?不(?! ?要)"
mandarin_exclusion_regex[mandarin_exclusion_phrases == "可不"] <- "可 ?不(?! ?可)"

# Match an excluded expression at a word or punctuation boundary.
mandarin_exclusion_pattern <- paste0(
  "(?<![\\p{L}\\p{N}])(?:",
  paste(mandarin_exclusion_regex, collapse = "|"),
  ")(?![\\p{L}\\p{N}])"
)

# A-not-A: a word starting with character X (not a negator), then 不/没/沒,
# then X again. Matches 是不是, 是 不 是, 有没有, 要 不 要, 喜欢 不 喜欢.
mandarin_a_not_a_pattern <-
  "(?<![\\p{L}\\p{N}])(?![不没沒])(\\p{L})\\S* ?[不没沒] ?\\1"

# Step 1: flag A-not-A questions (they count as negation).
# Step 2: remove excluded phrases.
# Step 3: negation if any 不/没/沒 is left, or it is an A-not-A question.
mandarin_code_negation <- function(data) {
  data %>%
    mutate(
      gloss_text = coalesce(as.character(gloss), ""),
      a_not_a = str_detect(gloss_text, mandarin_a_not_a_pattern),
      gloss_no_exclusions = str_squish(
        str_remove_all(gloss_text, mandarin_exclusion_pattern)
      ),
      negation = a_not_a | str_detect(gloss_no_exclusions, mandarin_negators)
    ) %>%
    select(-gloss_text)
}

mandarin_utterances <- mandarin_code_negation(mandarin_utterances)
```

# Classify Negation

Classifies negation at the utterance level and maps its category and scope to token rows in `mandarin_tokens`.

## Classify Utterance Scope

Applies `classify_negation` and `mandarin_negation_rules` to assign `negation_rule` and `negation_type` to negation utterances.

```{r mandarin_categorization}
# ---- Word lists ----
# Removed from the END of the utterance (了 and 的 included).
mandarin_particles <- c(
  "了", "的", "啊", "呀", "哇", "哪", "吧", "嘛", "啦", "哦", "喔", "噢",
  "呢", "耶", "咯", "喽", "囉", "啰", "嘞", "哈"
)
# Removed from the START and the END.
mandarin_interjections <- c("嗯", "哎", "唉", "诶", "欸", "哼")
# Used only for 不 + new clause (不 妈妈 我 要). NOT removed from the end,
# because 不 能 打 妈妈 / 不 是 妈妈 use them as objects.
mandarin_address_terms <- c(
  "妈妈", "媽媽", "爸爸", "宝宝", "寶寶", "奶奶",
  "爷爷", "爺爺", "姐姐", "哥哥", "阿姨"
)
# A pronoun after the negator means a sentence (不 给 你), not a short answer.
mandarin_pronouns <- c(
  "我", "你", "妳", "他", "她", "它", "咱", "我们", "你们", "他们",
  "这", "那", "这个", "那个", "什么"
)
# POS tags allowed for the word after the negator.
mandarin_pos_allowed <- c("verb", "adj", "aux")

# Which rule leads to which type.
mandarin_negation_rules <- tribble(
  ~negation_rule,                 ~negation_type,
  "bare_negator",                 "discourse",   # 不, 没有, 没 了
  "negator_plus_verb",            "discourse",   # 不 要, 不 知道, 不 玩 了
  "bu_then_clause",               "discourse",   # 不 我 要 那个
  "bu_then_clause_with_negator",  "mixed",       # 不 我 不 要
  "question_ma",                  "sentential",  # 没有 吗
  "negator_not_first",            "sentential",  # 我 不 要, 是不是
  "more_content",                 "sentential",  # 不 玩 积木
  "pronoun_follows",              "sentential",  # 不 给 你
  "pos_not_verb_adj",             "sentential"   # 没有 人 (noun)
)

# ---- Classify ONE negation utterance; returns the rule name ----
# words: the words of gloss_no_exclusions
# tags:  the matching POS tags, or NULL when the tags can't be used
classify_negation <- function(words, tags = NULL) {
  if (is.null(tags)) tags <- rep(NA_character_, length(words))
  words <- str_replace(words, "^不{2,}$", "不")  # joined 不不 -> 不

  # Questions ending in 吗 are sentential: 没有 吗, 不是 吗
  if (words[length(words)] %in% c("吗", "嗎")) return("question_ma")

  # Step 1a: drop interjections at the start (嗯 不 -> 不)
  while (length(words) > 0 && words[1] %in% mandarin_interjections) {
    words <- words[-1]
    tags  <- tags[-1]
  }
  # Step 1b: drop particles, 了 and interjections at the end
  ending_words <- c(mandarin_particles, mandarin_interjections)
  while (length(words) > 0 && words[length(words)] %in% ending_words) {
    words <- words[-length(words)]
    tags  <- tags[-length(tags)]
  }
  # Step 1c: collapse exact repeats (不 要 不 要 -> 不 要, 不 不 不 -> 不)
  n <- length(words)
  for (m in seq_len(n %/% 2)) {
    if (n %% m == 0 && identical(words, rep(words[1:m], n / m))) {
      words <- words[1:m]
      tags  <- tags[1:m]
      break
    }
  }

  # Step 2: the negator must come first; otherwise it is inside a sentence
  if (length(words) == 0 || !str_detect(words[1], "^[不没沒]")) return("negator_not_first")

  # Drop extra leading 不 (不 不 我 要 -> 不 我 要)
  while (length(words) > 1 && words[1] == "不" && words[2] == "不") {
    words <- words[-1]
    tags  <- tags[-1]
  }

  # 不 + a new clause: 不 我 要 那个 ("No, I want that one").
  # If the new clause has its own negator (不 我 不 要), it is mixed.
  if (words[1] == "不" && length(words) > 1 &&
      words[2] %in% c(mandarin_pronouns, mandarin_address_terms)) {
    if (any(str_detect(words[-(1:2)], "[不没沒]"))) return("bu_then_clause_with_negator")
    return("bu_then_clause")
  }

  # Step 3: look at what follows the negator.
  # 不要 -> 要, 不 知道 -> 知道, 没有 -> (nothing)
  after_negator <- c(str_remove(words[1], "^(?:[没沒]有|[不没沒])"), words[-1])
  after_tags <- tags[-1]  # the negator word's own tag isn't needed

  if (all(after_negator == "")) return("bare_negator")
  if (nchar(paste(after_negator, collapse = "")) > 2) return("more_content")
  if (any(words[-1] %in% mandarin_pronouns)) return("pronoun_follows")
  if (any(!is.na(after_tags) & !after_tags %in% mandarin_pos_allowed)) return("pos_not_verb_adj")
  "negator_plus_verb"
}

# ---- Apply to the data ----
mandarin_code_negation_type <- function(data) {
  gloss_clean <- str_squish(coalesce(as.character(data$gloss), ""))
  pos_clean   <- str_squish(coalesce(as.character(data$part_of_speech), ""))
  words <- str_split(str_squish(data$gloss_no_exclusions), " ")
  tags  <- str_split(pos_clean, " ")

  # Use the POS tags only when there is one tag per word and no exclusion
  # phrase was removed (removing one would shift the words out of line).
  data$pos_usable <- pos_clean != "" &
    lengths(tags) == lengths(str_split(gloss_clean, " ")) &
    data$gloss_no_exclusions == gloss_clean

  # Only negation utterances get a rule; the rest stay NA.
  negation_rule <- rep(NA_character_, nrow(data))
  for (i in which(data$negation)) {
    negation_rule[i] <- classify_negation(
      words[[i]], if (data$pos_usable[i]) tags[[i]] else NULL
    )
  }
  data$negation_rule <- negation_rule

  data %>%
    select(-any_of("negation_type")) %>%  # safe to rerun
    left_join(mandarin_negation_rules, by = "negation_rule")
}

mandarin_utterances <- mandarin_code_negation_type(mandarin_utterances)
count(mandarin_utterances, negation_type)
```

## Map Scope to Tokens

Splits `mandarin_utterances$gloss` into `mandarin_tokens` and assigns `negation_category` and token-level `negation_scope` while masking excluded phrases.

```{r mandarin_splittoken}
# Mark tokens covered by an exclusion phrase. Each matched character is
# replaced with a placeholder and spaces are kept, so the masked string
# splits into exactly the same tokens as the original.
mandarin_mask <- "\uE000"

mandarin_tokens <- mandarin_utterances %>%
  mutate(
    .gloss  = str_squish(coalesce(as.character(gloss), "")),
    .masked = str_replace_all(
      .gloss, mandarin_exclusion_pattern,
      function(m) str_replace_all(m, "\\S", mandarin_mask)
    ),
    token        = str_split(.gloss, " "),
    token_masked = str_split(.masked, " "),
    .pos         = str_split(str_squish(coalesce(as.character(part_of_speech), "")), " "),
    # Keep per-token POS only when there is one tag per token
    token_pos = map2(.pos, token, function(p, t) {
      if (length(p) == length(t)) p else rep(NA_character_, length(t))
    })
  ) %>%
  select(-.gloss, -.masked, -.pos) %>%
  unnest(c(token, token_masked, token_pos)) %>%
  filter(token != "") %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  mutate(token_order = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup()

# One token = at most one negation occurrence (same unit as English).
mandarin_tokens <- mandarin_tokens %>%
  mutate(
    token_excluded = str_detect(token_masked, paste0("^", mandarin_mask, "+$")),
    .is_neg = !token_excluded & str_detect(token, "[不没沒]"),
    negation_category = case_when(
      !.is_neg ~ NA_character_,
      str_detect(token, "不") ~ "bu",
      TRUE ~ "mei"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-token_masked, -.is_neg) %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  mutate(
    # For "mixed" (不 我 不 要): negators before the new clause are
    # discourse, negators inside the clause are sentential.
    .clause_started = cumsum(token %in% c(mandarin_pronouns, mandarin_address_terms)) > 0,
    negation_scope = case_when(
      is.na(negation_category) ~ NA_character_,
      negation_type == "mixed" & !.clause_started ~ "discourse",
      negation_type == "mixed" ~ "sentential",
      TRUE ~ negation_type
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-.clause_started)


# Sanity checks: every negator token should sit in a negation utterance.
count(mandarin_tokens, token_excluded, negation_category)
count(mandarin_tokens, negation_category, has_type = !is.na(negation_type))
```
# Save Processed Data

Saves `mandarin_tokens` to `mandarin_data/processed_data/mandarin_tokens_processed.feather` for downstream counts and plots.

```{r save_processed_data}
write_feather(
  mandarin_tokens %>%
    select(-any_of(c("negation", "a_not_a", "negation_rule", "negation_type",
                     "gloss_no_exclusions", "pos_usable"))) %>%
    rename(utterance_id = id,
           utterance_gloss = gloss, gloss = token,
           utterance_pos = part_of_speech, part_of_speech = token_pos),
  file.path(mandarin_processed_dir, "mandarin_tokens_processed.feather")
)
```
